newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian current account gap narrows in February.
newsitem.headline: Romanian current account gap narrows in February.

text.p: Romania's current account deficit was "four times lower" in February than an estimated $400 million in January, central bank (BNR) vice-governor Vlad Soare said on Friday.
"Estimates based on data provided by banks put the current account deficit at about $400 million in January," Soare told a news conference.
"But it (the deficit) narrowed last month when it was four times lower than in January," Soare added.

Latest BNR data put the current account deficit at $284 million last November, with the 11-month gap figure at $1.59 billion. Data on December were not available, but estimates by the BNR put the 1996 current account gap at $2.3 billion.

Soare said the high current account deficit in January had put pressure on the leu currency earlier this year, which dropped to an all-time low of 9,000 to the dollar. A cash-heavy money market added to the problem, he said.
The leu was some 5,000 to the dollar by the New Year.

But over the past weeks the leu has suffered an upward correction. It trades now near 6,900 to the dollar following the BNR's tough monetary policies and a move to eliminate market curbs imposed by the former leftist government in 1996.
Last month, the central bank decided to restore the local dealer status to 24 banks, which now act as market makers along with other four which previously controlled the market.

Romania plans to slash its current acoount deficit to $1.4 billion this year from an estimated $2.3 billion in 1996, in a bid to restore macro-economic stability, boost market reforms and win international support.
